subject: Clarify billing audit safeguards when a DSR requests account erasure
messages:
From: Lina Gomez <lina.gomez@acme.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 14 Jun 2026 14:03:00 +0000
Subject: Question: invoices & usage logs if user requests erasure

Kim —

Quick question from our audit team: Acme is preparing for a regulatory request and we're clarifying how Redwood handles deletion requests (DSRs) that ask for full user erasure. Specifically: if an end user requests erasure, will invoices, billing line-items, or aggregated usage records that reference that user be retained for accounting/audit purposes? Our auditors want the pathway documented (what stays, what is redacted, how long).

I attached a redacted invoice sample so you can see what fields they're looking at. Can you confirm the standard Redwood approach and any exception process? Also let us know if we need a formal attestation for our records.

Thanks,
Lina Gomez
Finance Controller, Acme Corp
[Attachment: acme-invoice-sample.pdf (PDF)]

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
To: Lina Gomez <lina.gomez@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 10:27:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Question: invoices & usage logs if user requests erasure

Hi Lina —

Thanks for the clear example. Short answer: Redwood preserves accounting artifacts (invoices, transaction ledger entries, reconciliations) needed for statutory accounting and audits even when a DSR requests erasure, but we limit retained PII to the minimum required and apply redaction where possible.

Key points:
- Invoices and billing line-items are part of the accounting ledger and are retained to meet financial recordkeeping obligations (GAAP/local tax).
- When a DSR is received we evaluate whether the requested data is needed to satisfy an accounting obligation; if it is, we place those records on an accounting retention exception and do not delete them.
- We will redact direct identifiers (email addresses, names) from copies used exclusively for audit traces when feasible, but legal/finance needs may require maintaining a linkage internally.
- Retention windows for accounting exceptions are driven by local regulation (typical range: 6–10 years) and our finance policy; for most customers the ledger/invoice artifacts are kept for 7 years.

Operationally, Marissa from Finance will own creating the retention exception and recording the justification (deal id, authority, retention period). We can provide a one‑page attestation that describes the exception and the fields preserved. I've attached a quick exception matrix that shows what we keep and recommended redactions.

Next steps:
1) Marissa will open an accounting exception and put the relevant documents behind the exception label.
2) We'll produce an attestation for Acme with the retention period and redaction notes.
3) If you need a signed statement, let us know, and we can route to legal for approval.

Will loop Marissa on the operational details below.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Director, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood-dsr-invoice-exception-matrix.xlsx]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Cc: Lina Gomez <lina.gomez@acme.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Jun 2026 08:04:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Question: invoices & usage logs if user requests erasure

Folks —

Operational checklist (Finance):
- Create accounting exception record: reference deal ACME-2026-09 and attach the redacted invoice sample.
- Populate retention rationale: statutory audit + tax obligations.
- Set retention window: 7 years from invoice date (standard; escalate if Acme needs longer).
- Mark the record with limited access: finance/legal only.
- Produce a PDF attestation describing the scope and fields retained; include a signature line for Redwood Legal if Acme requires a signed copy.

Lina — I'll open the HubSpot ticket and an internal retention ticket. Please confirm whether Acme needs the attestation signed or if a standard signed letter from Finance is sufficient.

HubSpot reference: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/deal/ACME-2026-09
Internal doc (for reference): https://docs.redwood.com/internal/dsr-retention-guidance

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Manager, Finance
Redwood Inference

Appreciate it,
